target_audience: University freshmen and AP Calculus students

sections.title: The Mystery of the Tangled Equation
sections.content: Introduce the difference between explicit functions (y = f(x)) and implicit equations where x and y are intertwined. Use a visual 'Function Machine' metaphor: an explicit function is a clear conveyor belt, while an implicit equation is a tangled knot where you can't easily isolate the output (y).
sections.example: Compare a simple 'Explicit' line (y = 2x + 3) with an 'Implicit' circle (x² + y² = 25). Show that for the circle, solving for y requires a ± square root, creating two separate functions instead of one cohesive rule.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Chain Rule 'Sidekick'
sections.content: Briefly review the Chain Rule, specifically how to differentiate a term containing 'y' with respect to 'x'. Explain that because y is a function of x (y(x)), whenever we differentiate a y-term, we must multiply by the 'inner derivative' dy/dx.
sections.example: Visualizing the 'Inner Layer': d/dx[y³] = 3y² · (dy/dx). Use an animation of a nested doll (Matryoshka) where the inner doll is labeled 'dy/dx'.

sections.title: The Strategy: The 'Level Playing Field'
sections.content: Present the core logic: We treat both sides of the equation equally by applying the d/dx operator to everything. Emphasize that we are looking for the rate of change (slope) without needing to untangle the equation first.
sections.example: Imagine a balance scale. If we apply the 'differentiation tool' to the left pan, we must apply it to the right pan to keep the relationship valid.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Walkthrough: The Circular Track
sections.content: Differentiate the circle equation x² + y² = 25 step-by-step. 1) Differentiate each term (2x + 2y·dy/dx = 0). 2) Group all terms containing dy/dx on one side. 3) Factor out dy/dx. 4) Divide to isolate dy/dx.
sections.example: Character: 'Calculus Cat' is walking on a circular track. At point (3, 4), what is his slope? Using our result dy/dx = -x/y, the slope is -3/4. Show a visual tangent line touching the circle at that exact point.

sections.title: Visualizing the Slope Field
sections.content: Show why implicit differentiation is powerful. It allows us to find the slope at any point (x, y) on complex curves like ellipses or hyperbola-shaped tracks, even where the vertical line test fails.
sections.example: A 'Rollercoaster Loop' (Folium of Descartes). Animate a point moving along the curve, showing the tangent line rotating in real-time based on the dy/dx formula derived implicitly.

sections.title: Final Summary & Pro-Tips
sections.content: Summarize the 3 Golden Rules: 1) Differentiate everything. 2) Remember the 'dy/dx' tag for y-terms. 3) Solve for dy/dx using algebra. Mention that this is the foundation for Related Rates problems.
sections.example: A quick-check checklist appears on screen: 'Did I use the Chain Rule on y?' 'Did I differentiate the constant (it becomes 0)?' 'Is dy/dx isolated?'
